newsitem.title: UK: FOUR OIL COMPANIES SHARE FIRST GERMAN CRUDE SALE.
newsitem.headline: FOUR OIL COMPANIES SHARE FIRST GERMAN CRUDE SALE.

text.p: Four European oil companies shared the first tranche of crude sold by the German government from strategic reserves, trading sources said on Wednesday.
German oil refiner RWE-DEA, Anglo-Dutch major Royal Dutch/Shell, Sweden's Preem Petroleum and Swiss-based Petrotrade submitted winning bids for the oil, they said.
Preem was awarded 1.3 million barrels, Shell Rotterdam 520,000 barrels, Petrotrade 520,000 barrels and RWE-DEA's trading arm Rheinoel 460,000 barrels.
British Petroleum Co Plc, reported on Tuesday as having won part of the volume, was not successful, the sources said.
All four winners were expected to take the oil into their own refining systems for testing and analysis.
"It will be going into the refinery. It's a mixture of crudes and we want to see exactly what's there," said one of the successful bidders.
The Hamburg-based oil supply agency EBV sold the 2.8 million barrels of high sulphur crude in the first of a series of tenders planned to raise money to plug holes in government finances.
Tender winners have until the end of August to lift the crude, typically a mixture of Iranian Heavy, Saudi Light and Iraqi Kirkuk, to lift the crude.

Trade sources said the RWE-DEA barrels would probably be pumped via pipeline to its Wesseling refinery. The other companies are expected to load the crude onto tankers at the northern port of Wilhelmshaven.
Earlier this summer Bonn said it hoped to raise 400 million marks ($215 million) this year and 500 million marks in 1998 by selling oil stockpiled in salt caverns since the late 1970s.
A government spokeswoman would not reveal details of the winners or the prices paid, but said the first tender had raised the expected revenue.
"The profits corresponded with expectations," she said.
EBV is expected to announce shortly a second tender closing around the middle of September, traders said.
